a-failed-run-is-loud <- templates/backup/backup.sh.erb:31: the tar line writes $BACKDIR/$FILEPREFIX-<date>.tar.gz, so a full one-page tmpfs over /opt/puppet-infrastructure/backup/sysmon makes it fail while the directory stays writable; the non-zero exit, the ERROR line on stderr and via logger -t backup-$FILEPREFIX (journalctl -t backup-sysmon.p8test.invalid) and the exit before the retention loop are local change #15 (current template lines 33-40, row 15 in local_changes.md), not baseline text; the planted archive dated 12 days is older than DAYS=10*1-1=9 (baseline 22-23, 35-37), so its survival shows retention was skipped. mutates covers the mount, the planted file, the script run and /run/p8test-sysmon-fail; the effect reads the recorded rc/stderr, the journal and the directory, not the action's output

purpose covered: Purpose (nightly gzip tar of sysmon::basedir into sysmon::backdir, keeping sysmon::backdays days) matches sysmon_backup.pp:1-13 and the backup define/template. Checks test: script installed root 0755 with the Hiera values (basedir, prefix sysmon::address, backdir, NC 10, compression true); root crontab 0 23 * * * for the script; the backup directory declared (local change #14) root 0755; a by-hand run exits 0 and writes a dated gzip archive that passes gzip -t and restores p8test.txt byte for byte; retention deletes only the prefix's file older than 9 days and keeps the 5-day one and the other prefix's 30-day file; a run that cannot write fails loudly and keeps old archives (local change #15). Uncovered, honestly: cron actually firing at 23:00 (phase3.py has no step that waits for or advances the node's cron schedule; the entry and the script it names are both tested) and compression false (one Hiera fixture per set leaves sysmon::compression unset; probes may not change the master's Hiera). EXCLUDEDIRS and TARGETUSER are empty constants in the template, so the exclude and chown branches are not outcomes of this class.
